subject: ent
title: Deep neck space infections

steps.tx: Deep neck infections spread along fascial planes from teeth (commonest), tonsils, salivary glands and foreign bodies, threatening airway, mediastinum, carotid and jugular structures. **Ludwig angina** is bilateral submandibular space cellulitis (usually odontogenic from lower molars) with woody floor of mouth, raised displaced tongue, drooling and airway obstruction risk, needing airway first (awake tracheostomy readiness), CT with contrast only when airway safe, broad antibiotics and surgical drainage with dental source removal.
steps.say: Woody mouth floor pushing tongue up is Ludwig angina: airway before scan, drain and pull the tooth.

steps.tx: **Retropharyngeal abscess** in young children (nodes draining nasopharynx, regressing by school age) causes fever, neck stiffness, torticollis, drooling and stridor mimicking epiglottitis or meningitis; adults get it from foreign body perforation, trauma or vertebral osteomyelitis spread. Parapharyngeal (lateral pharyngeal) abscess shows trismus, tonsil medial displacement and neck swelling, with carotid sheath posterior compartment risks: jugular thrombosis (Lemierre fusobacterial sepsis after pharyngitis in adolescents), carotid erosion blowout and lower cranial neuropathies.
steps.say: Stiff necked drooling toddler may have pus behind pharynx. Throat infection then septic jugular clot is Lemierre.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Imaging and airway sequencing rules care: unstable airway goes to theatre for controlled securing (fibreoptic or tracheostomy under local) before imaging trips; stable patients get contrast CT neck (and chest if mediastinitis suspected: widened mediastinum, chest pain, crepitus). Descending necrotising mediastinitis carries high mortality needing thoracic surgery drainage. Necrotising fasciitis (pain out of proportion, bullae, crepitus, rapid spread, diabetic hosts) demands immediate wide debridement beyond antibiotics.
steps.say: Secure airway first, then scan. Pus descending to chest needs chest surgeons too.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Complication vigilance continues after drainage: carotid blowout heralded by sentinel bleed, jugular thrombophlebitis septic emboli, mediastinitis, aspiration and sepsis. Source control (tooth extraction, foreign body removal, tonsil drainage pathways) plus cultures directed antibiotics (streptococci, anaerobes, staphylococci cover patterns) and HDU monitoring complete care. Diabetes and immunocompromise lower thresholds for imaging and surgery.
steps.say: Watch for warning bleeds from carotid after neck pus. Treating pus without removing tooth fails.
